title: refactor(app-shell): Studio's object settings panel picks with the shared Select (objectui#11865)
body:
Part of #11865
Clause-②: no

The object settings slice of objectui#11865 (claim 6064876007): the five browser-native select elements on Studio's object Settings tab become the shared Radix `Select`. The card stays open for the other native selects. The earlier slices are objectui#11934 (the Group panel), objectui#11976 (the validation editor) and objectui#11990 (*Explain access*).

## What changed

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`: one module-private `SettingsPicker`, drawn with the shared `Select` from `@object-ui/components`, renders all five pickers: the internal sharing model, the external sharing model, the name field, the lifecycle field, and the highlight fields' "+ Add field…". It follows the validation editor's `RulePicker`. Items carry their option's index, so the options whose value is `''` ("not set", "auto-derived", "auto-detect", "+ Add field…") need no empty `SelectItem`. A stored value that none of the options carries gets an item of its own. Each caller turns the picked value into the same patch as before: the mapping expressions are the native `onChange` bodies, with the event's value replaced by the picked value.
- Each labelled picker stays inside its wrapping label element, which names the trigger as it named the native control. The "+ Add field…" picker had no label and still has none. The two OWD triggers keep their test ids (`owd-internal-select`, `owd-external-select`); the other three gain `name-field-select`, `stage-field-select` and `highlight-add-select`.
- Untouched: the Basics inspector, the capability checkboxes, the highlight chips and their remove buttons, the descriptions under the OWD dials, the props and the exports. No i18n key is added: the panel's set of `engine.*` keys is identical to the base's (diffed).
- `ObjectSettingsPanel.sharedSelect-11865.test.tsx` (new), 35 tests.
- `ObjectSettingsPanel.test.tsx`: the five OWD-dial cases that drove the native control (option list, pick, clear, external default, external clear) now open and pick through the trigger, and check the same things.
- `StudioDesignSurface.servedDraftTakenAsIs-10765.test.tsx`: its Data pillar case read the dial's `value`. The trigger is a button, whose `value` is `''` whatever the dial holds, so that assertion would have passed vacuously. It now reads the trigger's text: the unset label is shown and the published `private` label is not.
- `.changeset/11865-object-settings-shared-select.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.

## Hypotheses

- **H1, value parity: held.** A scratch probe (uncommitted, deleted) fired a `change` event on every option of each native select on base `0bbb67b9a` and recorded the patch. The new suite's 24-row table pins every option of every picker against those literals, compared as JSON text, with the keys that hold `undefined` named:
  - each "not set", "auto-derived" and "auto-detect" option writes its key holding `undefined`;
  - "None" writes `stageField: false`;
  - a field writes its name, and an added highlight is appended to the list;
  - "+ Add field…" writes nothing.

  A table-coverage test pins each picker's listed options in order. Caveat: the probe's `change` event fired for the current option too, so the re-pick rows (no write) pin the primitive, not a browser reading of the native control.
- **H2, labels, keyboard and read-only: held.** The probe read each native select's accessible name on base. On head each trigger computes the same name: the four label texts, and `''` for the "+ Add field…" picker on both. Enter opens a picker, and Enter on an option selects it. The panel has a read-only state: `disabled`, which `StudioDesignSurface` passes from its read-only flag. In it, the four triggers are disabled, wear the primitive's own `disabled:` classes, and do not open. The "+ Add field…" picker is not drawn, as on base.
- **H3, a stored value outside the options: held.** Each of these is shown in the trigger: a name field naming a missing field, a lifecycle field naming a field that is not a select field, and sharing models neither dial offers (`full`, `read_write`). The native control showed its first option there. The missing name field is listed first, and re-picking it writes nothing.
- **H4, first-load bytes: byte-neutral locally.** On `e02c4c116`: `apps/console` `vite build` plus `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`, on head and on the same tree with the panel at its base blob (landing and restore proven by hash).
  - Both legs print `Console eager closure is 3311.2 KB gzipped across 337 of 2459 chunks (budget: 3312.0 KB, headroom: 0.8 KB).`
  - `eagerGzipBytes` is 3390714 on both legs, and `eagerRawBytes` is equal. The only eager entry that differs is the entry chunk's file-name hash; its bytes are identical.
  - The panel ships in the lazy `studioBuilder` chunk on both legs.

  The budget bot's reading on this PR is the authority.

## Reverse leg

With the implementation committed, the panel was written from its base blob (its hash equals the base blob: 5 native select elements, 0 `SettingsPicker`). Then the new suite, `ObjectSettingsPanel.test.tsx` and the served-draft suite ran: `Tests 41 failed | 11 passed (52)`.
- Red: all 35 new pins, the five rewritten OWD-dial cases, and the served-draft Data pillar case.
- Green: the eight untouched cases of `ObjectSettingsPanel.test.tsx` and the served-draft suite's three other cases.

That is the direction the suite header predicts. The restore, `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap, is proven: the hash equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes.

## Gates (on `e02c4c116`)

- The seven suites that mount the real panel, repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run`: `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 61 passed (61)`. `DataPillar.hiddenSystemFields-11780.test.tsx` stubs the panel and is not among them.
- `column-identity.ratchet` and `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 18 passed (18)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, after the app-shell dependency closure build: exit 0. By `--listFilesOnly`, the panel is in the main program, and the panel and the three touched suites are in the test program.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the four touched `.tsx` files: exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new) and `check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- Also exit 0: the changeset fixed, overwrite and claims gates, `pending-changeset-literals`, `test-path-roots`, the three vi-mock gates, `phantom-deps`, `unreferenced-sources`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `i18n-drift`, `metadata-write-doors`, `esm-specifiers`, `self-import`, lint coverage, type-check coverage, `handler-key-reads` and `designer-field-key-parity`. `component-surface-parity` and `i18n-dead-keys` also exit 0; both are report-only.
- Declared to CI: the full `pnpm test` farm and repo-wide `pnpm lint`.

## Acceptance notes

- The "+ Add field…" picker has no accessible name, on base and on head: it has no label, and this slice keeps each control's name as it was. Naming it, for example by the "Highlight fields" caption, is not in this slice. Noted, not filed.
- The name-field and "+ Add field…" lists hold every field of the object, so they can be long. They use `Select`, as the claim directs and as the earlier slices measured. `Select` jumps to an option by its typed leading letters.
- Browser: not measured in this slice. Keyboard and read-only behaviour are pinned in the test DOM only.
